svg.title: Bond and AD/CVD Exposure Bands
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-bond-and-adcvd-exposure-bands; chapter number: 4; title: Bond and AD/CVD Exposure Bands; subtitle: From the $50K bond floor to $22M of stacked step-up exposure; caption: A bond is a revenue guarantee, not insurance. Size it from rolling 365-day duties, taxes and fees, and skip intermediate sizes rather than stepping up one size at a time.; assumptions note: Values are in USD millions. Bond sufficiency is 10% of annual duties, taxes and fees with a $50K minimum. The AD/CVD bucket uses the single container example the speaker gave.; note: Sources are Trade Risk Guaranty for bond sizing and step-up exposure and Ask The Customs Manager for the AD/CVD container example.; chart type: stacked_comparison; unit: USD millions; total range: $0.05M bond floor to $22M stacked exposure; buckets: label: Minimum continuous bond; low: 0.05; high: 0.05; notes: $50K floor; a $50K bond covers $500K of duties, taxes and fees.; label: AD/CVD bill on one aluminum container; low: 0.05; high: 0.15; notes: A $50K container draws a $150K duty bill; AD/CVD runs 50% to over 300% of value.; label: Mid-term step-up path; low: 5; high: 10; notes: $5M to $7M to $10M; one-size bumps fail within 12 months nine times out of 10.; label: Stacked exposure from stepping; low: 22; high: 22; notes: The step-up path stacks $22M; start at $10M or skip $7M instead.
